segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Two prior flights, same fault, both cleared themselves... My read was, this is a known quantity... So there wasn't a strong pull toward digging further.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats repeated self-clearing fault history and MEL disposition as evidence that further inspection is unnecessary for dispatch.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My first thought honestly was, there it is again, exactly like the tech log said... keep the climb going... at the time it felt like a clear pattern rather than a limited sample.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant predicts benign future fault behavior with high confidence from a brief, small-sample pattern.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I weighted his extensive time on type... more heavily than a step-by-step review of the QRH sequence... With him, the track record does a lot of the work.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant grades the captain more favorably because of seniority and track record instead of independently verifying procedural compliance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I told him I didn't think that applied to me... that kind of thing is more of a risk for someone earlier in their check-airman career... For me, I trust the process I've built.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant dismisses a peer's critique of his own judgment while attributing similar susceptibility to less experienced evaluators.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If the connector fault had failed completely instead of intermittently, sure, that reframes everything... none of this proves anything one way or the other about the calls I made.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a substantive retrospective reflection, but outcome bias is not part of the exhaustive hidden manifest.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Probably not much, if I'm honest. Maybe I'd log the climb flicker more formally. But the information I had pointed the same direction every time I looked at it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explains what he would change under the same information; no additional hidden instance is manifested.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Pre-departure dispatch acceptance based on repeated self-clearing ADIRU fault history
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Treats repeated self-clearing of an ADIRU fault as proof of continued safety absent new diagnostic confirmation, used to justify accepting the aircraft at dispatch.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring and adjustment is a related but distinct construct. It is not an approved equivalent of Normalcy Bias, even though both can involve over-weighting prior benign information.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the relevant self-clearing history, absence of new confirmation, dispatch-risk operation, and treating the unresolved recurrence as a non-issue. The label remains incorrect, but the stated mechanism fully matches.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is verbatim, correctly attributed, and directly supports the dispatch reasoning.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: In-flight predictive judgment to continue the climb after a transient ADIRU disagree indication
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Expresses unwarranted confidence in predicting the fault's future behavior from a brief, small-sample pattern rather than validated diagnostic data.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a related but distinct construct. The finding emphasizes selective confirmation of an existing benign model rather than the hidden construct's central feature of high-confidence prediction from a small sample.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures matching the new event to prior benign observations and underweighting a worsening-fault alternative, but it does not fully express the hidden predictive-confidence mechanism or its sample-size distortion.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is verbatim, correctly attributed, and directly localizes the finding to the climb-phase reasoning.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change; there are no low-confidence identified occurrences.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Adding two candidates produces no new true positives and adds two duplicate false positives, lowering strict F1 to 0.1818 and mechanism-first F1 to 0.5455.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: Perfect high-confidence segment detection: all four positive segments are detected. At moderate-inclusive thresholds, one negative segment is falsely flagged by Outcome bias.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Only Bias Blind Spot is an exact instance-level match. The other three positive episodes receive near-neighbor labels, yielding strict recall 0.25 and high-and-moderate F1 0.2222.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Three of four hidden mechanisms are recovered with correct localization, including the Normalcy Bias and Experience Bias mechanisms under near-neighbor labels. Illusion of validity is only partially captured by Confirmation bias.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Candidates add no true positives. One is a useful abstention and one is mechanism-aligned, but both are duplicates of an already identified climb-phase claim under the candidate-priority rule and therefore add false positives at the fourth threshold.
main_failure_modes: Near-neighbor labels were used instead of the hidden Normalcy Bias and Experience Bias target labels.
Confirmation bias did not fully capture the hidden small-sample predictive-confidence mechanism.
Outcome bias was reported on a negative segment outside the hidden manifest.
Candidate findings duplicated an already identified episode rather than improving coverage.
main_strengths: All four hidden reasoning segments were localized correctly at the segment level.
Evidence quotations were valid, verbatim, and correctly attributed.
Bias Blind Spot was identified with exact label and mechanism.
The anchoring and halo findings captured two hidden mechanisms fully under the mechanism-first scorecard.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run has strong segment detection and substantial mechanism recovery but weak strict taxonomy performance. Its high-and-moderate mechanism-first F1 is 0.6667, compared with strict F1 0.2222, indicating a sizable taxonomy-label gap.
